title: The No Contact Rule After a Breakup: How Long and How — cv.cm
description: The no contact rule explained: why a break from your ex helps you heal, how long to keep it, how to handle kids or work, and what to do if your ex reaches out.
h1: What is the no contact rule, and does it work?
answer: The no contact rule means a set period after a breakup with no messages, calls, likes, story views or visits with your ex. It works for healing, not as a trick to win them back. Thirty days is a common starting point, not a magic number. If you share children, a home or a job, use low contact: polite, practical messages only.

sections.h: What the no contact rule is, and what it is not
body: After a breakup, many people keep a thin line open: a late-night message, a like on a photo, checking who viewed their story. The no contact rule closes that line for a while. People call it 断联 or 冷静期 in Chinese, 冷却期間 in Japanese, and contacto cero in Spanish.
In practice, no contact means you do not:

ul: Send messages, voice notes or stickers on any chat app.
Call, or answer just to hear their voice.
Like, comment on or view their posts and stories.
Ask mutual friends how they are, or send messages through them.
Go to places only to run into them.

body: What it is not: a strategy to make an ex miss you. Many websites sell no contact as a way to control the other person's feelings. That framing keeps you focused on them, which is the opposite of what the rule is for. Do it for yourself. If you later decide to reach out, you will do it with a clearer head.

The NHS lists the end of a relationship as a loss that can cause grief, much like other major losses. Grief needs time and room. Every new message from an ex restarts the hope and the hurt, so the healing clock keeps resetting.

Research on online contact points the same way. A study of 464 people (Marshall, 2012) found that those who kept checking an ex-partner's Facebook page reported more distress about the breakup, more negative feelings, more longing for the ex, and less personal growth. Staying friends online without checking all the time had mixed results. The checking was the clear problem.

No contact also helps you see the relationship as it was. When you are not reacting to their latest message, it becomes easier to notice the patterns that ended it, the part that was yours, and what you want next time.

sections.h: How long should no contact last?
body: Thirty days is a common starting point because it is long enough for the first wave of pain to ease, and short enough to feel possible. It is not a rule from research, and there is nothing special about day 31.

body: A good sign that no contact has done its job: you can think of them without a rush of hope or anger, and you no longer plan your day around whether they might message.

sections.h: How to do it, step by step

ol: Decide the length and write the end date down, or decide there is no end date.

If you want, send one short message so they are not confused: "I need some time without contact to heal. Please don't message me for a while. I wish you well." You do not owe this, and you do not need to explain more.
Mute and archive the chat. You do not have to block unless they keep contacting you or you cannot stop yourself.
Hide or unfollow their social media, and mute their close friends if their posts are a trigger.
Move photos and gifts into one folder or box out of sight. You do not need to delete or throw them away now.
Tell one or two friends what you are doing and ask them to not pass on news about your ex.
Plan for the hard moments before they happen.

body: Bad nights are when most people break no contact. Have a short plan ready:

ul: Write the message you want to send in a notes app, not in the chat. Read it the next morning.
Call or message a friend instead. Agree in advance that you can text them "bad night" any time.
Go for a walk, take a shower, or do something with your hands for 20 minutes. The urge usually passes.
Put your phone in another room an hour before sleep.
Avoid drinking alone. Alcohol makes late-night messages much more likely.

body: If you break no contact, do not punish yourself. Note what triggered it and start again. Progress is not lost because of one message.

sections.h: When you cannot cut all contact: low contact
body: Some people have to stay in touch: you share a child, a lease, a pet, a workplace or a class. In these cases use low contact. Keep messages short, polite and about practical things only. Do not add feelings, jokes or questions about their life.

body: If you share children and contact becomes hostile, some parents use a dedicated co-parenting app or email only, so that messages stay calm and on record.

sections.h: What to do if your ex reaches out
body: Your ex may message you during this time. You decide whether to reply. It is fine to not reply at all, and it is fine to reply once and keep your boundary.

body.note: If an ex keeps contacting you after you said stop, shows up at your home, threatens you, or tracks you, that is harassment, not love. Save the messages, tell people you trust, and contact local emergency services if you feel in danger. A domestic violence helpline, such as loveisrespect.org or thehotline.org in the US, or a local service where you live, can help you plan for safety.

faq.q: Does the no contact rule work to get an ex back?
faq.a: It is not meant to. Some exes reach out during no contact and many do not. It works well for its real purpose: helping you calm down, stop checking, and make clearer decisions.

faq.q: Should I tell my ex I am going no contact?
faq.a: You can, with one short and kind message, especially after a long relationship. You do not have to, and you should not use the announcement to start a new discussion.

faq.q: Does looking at their story count as breaking no contact?
faq.a: Yes, in practice. They may see that you viewed it, and it keeps you emotionally attached. Mute or hide their stories so you do not have to decide each time.

faq.q: Is no contact cruel or immature?
faq.a: Not when it is done honestly. Taking space to heal is healthy. It becomes unkind only when it is used to punish someone or to play mind games.
Muting is often enough. Block if they keep messaging after you asked for space, if contact feels unsafe, or if you keep breaking no contact and want to make it harder for yourself.
